title: Root norms equal the spectral value of a split monic polynomial
statement: Let $k$ be a normed field [def-weil-field], let $L$ be a field with a specified $k$-algebra structure, and let $N:L\to\mathbf R_{\ge0}$ be an algebra norm: it vanishes exactly at zero, satisfies $N(-x)=N(x)$, $N(x+y)\le N(x)+N(y)$, $N(xy)\le N(x)N(y)$, and $N(ax)=|a|N(x)$. Assume $N(1)=1$, $N(x+y)\le\max(N(x),N(y))$, and $N(x^n)=N(x)^n$ for every $n\ge1$. Let $p\in k[Z]$ be monic of degree $r\ge1$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring], and suppose its image in $L[Z]$ is $\prod_{a\in s}(Z-a)$ for a finite multiset $s$ of elements of $L$, with repetitions allowed. Then $s$ is nonempty and $\max_{a\in s}N(a)=\max_{0\le j<r}|p_j|^{1/(r-j)}$, where $p_j$ is the coefficient of $Z^j$. The right side is Mathlib\'s $\operatorname{spectralValue}(p)$.
